extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and counsel handling practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules the USPTO applies in disciplinary proceedings against registered patent/trademark practitioners: applicable regulatory provisions, examples of misconduct, mitigation considerations, sanctions, and reinstatement requirements. The document is an Amended Final Order implementing an Agreement and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b) via 10.23(c)(8) — failing to inform client of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(8) for failing to inform a client of correspondence received from the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies failing to communicate Notices (e.g., Notice to File Missing Parts, Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment, Notices of Non‑Compliant Amendment) to a client as a violation. Examples in the stipulation include not communicating a Notice to File Missing Parts, not timely informing the client of Office Actions, and not reporting abandonments. Such failures support discipline under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of a legal matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) for neglecting a legal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order treats allowing applications to become abandoned (through failure to respond to Office Actions) and failing to take steps reasonably necessary to avoid prejudice to a client as neglect. Examples include failing to respond to an Office Action causing abandonment and failing to report the abandonment to the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — thoroughness and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101: practitioner shall represent client with thoroughness and preparation reasonably necessary for the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites inadequate preparation/thoroughness (e.g., filing errors, non‑compliant amendments, failing to enter additional claims properly) as conduct contrary to this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103: practitioner shall be diligent in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lapses such as failing to timely respond to Office Actions, not following through on filings, or misleading the client regarding Office activity are cited as breaches of the duty of diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104 — communication with client
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104: practitioner shall communicate with a client as to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific communication failures are highlighted (e.g., not informing client about abandonments, petitions for revival, non‑compliant amendment notices, or the dates of Office Actions). The Order uses these examples to ground the communication violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115 — safekeeping client property and funds
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115: safekeeping client property and funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites improper invoicing and over‑charging for PTO fees (incorrect fee calculations, billing for more claims than filed, accepting client funds but not paying USPTO fees) as violations of the safekeeping/funds rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory jurisdiction to discipline (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions authorize the Director and OED to investigate, enter into settlement agreements, and impose discipline. The Order was issued pursuant to these statutes/regulations and related procedural rules (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark and other non‑patent matters for twelve (12) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement orders a 12‑month suspension beginning on the date the Final Order is signed; after nine months Respondent may seek reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, but remains suspended until a petition is granted. The Order also requires compliance with other conditions (exclusion from customer numbers/PKI, etc.) as part of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement conditions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for reinstatement include retaking/passing the Examination for Registration to Practice in Patent Cases before the USPTO, demonstrating good moral character and reputation, competency and learning in the law, and passing the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination with a scaled score ≥ 85.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states that any petition for reinstatement to practice in patent matters is predicated upon retaking and passing the Registration Examination, retaking and passing the MPRE with a scaled score equal to or greater than 85, and demonstrating good moral character, reputation, competency, and learning in the law. It also references compliance obligations under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.59 — compliance obligations between Respondent and OED
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order requires Respondent to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and requires the OED Director to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cross‑references reflect procedural requirements related to implementation of suspensions and publication of disciplinary orders (e.g., timing, notices, and publication protocols). The Order implements these obligations (e.g., dissociation of names, publishing Final Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI; restriction on obtaining Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates; Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the sanction, the Order requires technical/administrative steps to prevent the respondent from practicing (removing access tied to customer numbers and PKI) and prohibits obtaining new customer numbers until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary action (OED FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order prescribes public disclosure of the suspension and a model Official Gazette notice including the rule violations, factual basis (e.g., failing to communicate, allowing abandonment, over‑charging), and restitution. Publication is part of the remedy and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record in future proceedings and bearing of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record (including the Final Order) in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings; the OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly preserves the Office's ability to use the disciplinary record as aggravating evidence or to rebut future statements, and specifies that each party bears its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of practitioner misconduct that support discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific acts and omissions cited as the factual basis for discipline include: failing to communicate Notices to File Missing Parts, failing to communicate Office Actions in a timely manner, failing to respond to Office Actions resulting in abandonment, filing non‑compliant amendments (constructive election of another invention), billing for fees not paid to the USPTO, invoicing for more claims than filed, accepting payment without filing (trademark), and over‑charging client for USPTO fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples illustrate the types of conduct that violate the cited professional responsibility rules (communication, diligence, thoroughness, safekeeping of funds). The Order also notes mitigation (restitution in form of goods, cooperation, temporary cessation of taking new clients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in imposing discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigation considered includes restitution to the client (including goods such as an automobile), a cooperative attitude during investigation, and the respondent's statement that he is not accepting new clients until the investigation concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes these mitigating elements when setting the agreed sanction; restitution and cooperation are recognized but do not preclude suspension and reinstatement conditions.
